corrected_value.authors: Maloney, L. T., & Dal Martello, M. F.
corrected_value.title: Kin recognition and the perceived facial similarity of children

decision.quote: Facial similarity between individuals informs kinship judgments in third-party kin recognition. Indeed, one study found that similarity and kinship judgments encapsulate the same information (Maloney & Dal Martello, 2006). Yet, another study found that this is not the case when comparing adult face pairs of different sex (DeBruine et al., 2009). We replicated these studies to further clarify the role of facial similarity in kin recognition.
decision.reason: The authors explicitly replicate Maloney and Dal Martello's (2006) child-face kinship and similarity judgment study using a larger sample of 100 child face pairs (50 sibling pairs and 50 matched unrelated pairs) rated by 318 participants, applying Maloney and Dal Martello's thresholding model and directly comparing the correlation between similarity and kinship ratings, task accuracy, and age-difference effects against Maloney and Dal Martello (2006). The reference list confirms the exact identity (Journal of Vision, 2006, 6, 1047-1056, doi: 10.1167/6.10.4). The only shipped row (2285) is DeBruine et al. (2009, doi: 10.1016/j.visres.2008.09.025), a distinct study by different authors on adult faces (target 1), so report equivalence does not apply. The prior adjudication also found blind_right but used legacy corrected_value keys.
